subject.title: feat: add transactional rollback for managed updates

question: Should OpenClaw adopt confirmation-gated package-and-state rollback as the supported behavior for managed local-prefix npm Gateway updates, including the new optional Gateway confirmation tier?
rationale: The patch establishes a new availability, recovery, and control-plane contract whose acceptable failure mode and supported installation scope cannot be determined from implementation quality alone.

options.title: Sponsor the managed-install transaction
options.body: Keep the local-prefix npm scope, require real launchd/systemd proof for success and rollback, and review the Gateway compatibility contract before merge.

options.title: Narrow to pre-restart safety checks
options.body: Retain candidate verification and package retention but defer state rollback, probation, and confirmation semantics to a separately approved design.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Defer transactional rollback until maintainers define the supported update/recovery product contract and test environment.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the managed-install transaction
recommendation.body: Keep the local-prefix npm scope, require real launchd/systemd proof for success and rollback, and review the Gateway compatibility contract before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The available context identifies this person as the assigned implementer of the proposed transaction boundary; a broader current-main ownership trail was not available in the read-only review context.
